samples.summary: Serve mode accepts `--fault` but never forwards it to `observeAction`, so the whole seeded positive control is a silent no-op during exploration
samples.evidence:
The diff threads `fault` through `parseArgs` → `serve(browser, baseUrl, timeoutMs, fault)` → (nothing). At `packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:447-452` serve mode calls `observeAction(page, req.action, { baseUrl, timeoutMs, oracles, index: index++ })` — `fault` is NOT in the options object, so `runAction`'s new `?fault=` seed (line 244) is never applied on the serve path. Only `runAttempt` (line 472) passes it.

The bypassing chain is entirely out of the runner: `scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:1` `runHunt({..., fault})` → `exploreImpl(persona, brief, { repo, context, sessionLog, fault })` → `exploreUi`'s `openSession({ repoRoot: repo, fault })` → `scripts/agent/hunt-ui-session.mjs:112-120` spawns the runner with `--serve --port N --fault <id>`. The runner validates the id, stores it, and then drops it. So `node hunt-ui.mjs run --fault drop-second-char` — the documented end-to-end positive control that `runHunt` even announces as "FAULT INJECTION ACTIVE … this run is a positive control" (hunt-ui.mjs:923) — explores a CLEAN app while `runUiPlan`-based replay runs seeded. The explorer therefore finds nothing to propose (and, if it did, the claim observations and the seeded replay would diverge and be dropped as not-reproduced), so the funnel-level control silently proves nothing — exactly the failure mode the change exists to eliminate. The fix belongs on the new code: add `fault` to the options at line 447.

samples.summary: File header still asserts there is no `?fault=` query parameter and no test-only branch in the harness route — the same file and page.tsx now both add exactly that
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:14-16 reads "Faults are injected from the DRIVER, never from application code. There is no `?fault=` query parameter and no test-only branch in the harness route — the page under test is the page that ships". The diff adds `KNOWN_FAULTS`/`installFault` and `useFaultFromSearchParams` in packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:83-127, and the same verify file now navigates to `?fault=drop-second-char` at lines 296/305/311. The contract this comment describes no longer holds, and the header is the first thing a reader of this lane sees.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as described. serve() receives `fault` (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:415, called with args.fault at :523) but the serve loop's observeAction call at :447-452 omits `fault` from the options object, so observeAction's default null (line 332) applies and runAction never appends the `&fault=` seed (line 244) — unlike plan mode's runAttempt (line 472). The query-string seed is the only activation mechanism: the harness reads `fault` from window.location.search against a closed registry (src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:83-88), and no other path can supply it since the action vocabulary carries only `surface` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:160-162, hunt-ui-probe.mjs:115). A consumer outside the diff depends on the dropped value: hunt-ui-session.mjs:107-121 validates the id and spawns the runner with `--serve --port N --fault <id>`, reached via hunt-ui.mjs:307 openSession({ repoRoot: repo, fault }) from runHunt (hunt-ui.mjs:897, 938), which announces "FAULT INJECTION ACTIVE ... this run is a positive control" at :923, while the replay/verify path does seed (hunt-ui.mjs:1023-1024, 1135). Net effect: exploration runs a clean app while replay runs seeded, so the end-to-end positive control is a silent no-op and observations would diverge from replay. Real cross-module contract break (caller supplies a flag the callee ignores), in the blast-radius lane, major impact. No guard elsewhere compensates.
